reponse:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compact latent visual states for interleaved multi-modal chains
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Bagel, a unified model that both understands and generates images, to emit at each reasoning step a visual state of sixty-four learned latent tokens produced by a small compressor from the model's own image generator, instead of a full image re-encoded into thousands of tokens. The compressor and a decoder that maps the latent tokens back to pixels are trained jointly with the reasoning chain on synthetic maze navigation, jigsaw solving and geometry problems with ground-truth intermediate images, and the decoder is used at inference only to inspect the chain. We measure accuracy on held-out mazes, jigsaw puzzles and GeoQA, GenEval and WISE scores for text-to-image prompts that require reasoning, and the sequence length and throughput per chain.
CONTROLS: The same model with text-only chains, with direct answers and no chain, with full-image interleaving at the same number of training examples, with random latent tokens in place of the compressor output, and a pipeline that calls an external image generator per step.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Latent states should match full-image interleaving on accuracy at a fraction of the sequence length and beat text-only chains on navigation and jigsaw. If random latent tokens do as well, the visual state carries no information and the gain comes from extra computation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Encoding only what changed between successive visual states
PROPOSAL: We train Show-o to represent each intermediate visual state not as a full image but as the set of discrete image tokens that differ from the previous state, with their positions, so that a move in a maze or a swap in a jigsaw costs a handful of tokens while a complete redraw remains possible. A learned change detector decides which token positions to emit, and the model reconstructs the current state by applying the changes to the previous one in a small state cache outside the attention context. Training data come from simulated maze navigation, jigsaw solving and contour-to-landscape generation with rendered intermediate states. We report accuracy on held-out tasks, the average number of visual tokens per step, and the fidelity of the reconstructed states to the rendered ones.
CONTROLS: Full-image interleaving at equal training data, text-only chains, direct answers, a fixed random subset of token positions of the same size as the detector's choice, and the model with the state cache disabled so that changes must be inferred from context alone.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Change encoding should cut visual tokens per step by an order of magnitude on navigation and jigsaw with no loss of accuracy, and lose some fidelity on landscape generation where most of the image changes. If the random-subset variant matches it, position selection is not what matters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Keeping only the latest visual states inside the attention window
PROPOSAL: We modify the attention mask of a unified model, Janus-Pro extended with image generation of intermediate states, so that every token attends to the whole textual history but only to the visual tokens of the two most recent visual states, earlier visual states being evicted from the key-value cache. Text thus carries long-range logic and images carry the current state, which bounds the quadratic term of the chain. We fine-tune on synthetic maze navigation, jigsaw solving and geometry with rendered intermediate images, and on an instruction-based editing set where each edit step is a visual state. We report accuracy on held-out tasks, editing scores on ImgEdit, and wall-clock throughput per chain against chain length.
CONTROLS: Full attention over all visual states, a window of one and of four states, random eviction of the same number of visual tokens, text-only chains, and a pipeline with an external editor called per step.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The two-state window should match full attention on navigation and jigsaw, where only the current state matters, and fall behind on long editing chains that refer back to early states. If random eviction does as well, recency is not what the model relies on.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A staged curriculum for stable training of long interleaved chains
PROPOSAL: We train Bagel on interleaved reasoning in three stages: text-only chains on the target tasks, chains with a single visual state at the end, then chains with up to twelve visual states, moving to the next stage when validation loss on the current one plateaus. Within each stage the text and image losses are reweighted every few hundred steps so that their gradient norms stay within a fixed ratio, and the image loss uses a shorter denoising schedule for intermediate states than for final images. Data are synthetic maze navigation, jigsaw solving and contour-to-landscape chains with rendered intermediates. We track divergence events, gradient norm per modality, validation loss and held-out accuracy at every stage.
CONTROLS: Direct training on full chains at the same total number of examples, the curriculum with the stages in reverse order, the curriculum with fixed loss weights, and five seeds per configuration to count divergences.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The staged curriculum should reach lower validation loss with fewer divergences than direct training, and reverse ordering should be the worst. If fixed weights do as well as adaptive ones, the stabilising effect comes from ordering alone.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A simulator-grounded corpus of interleaved visual reasoning chains
PROPOSAL: We generate a training corpus in which each example pairs a problem with a chain alternating textual steps and rendered visual states produced by a simulator: grid mazes with the agent's path drawn step by step, jigsaw puzzles with pieces placed one at a time, topographic contour maps progressively turned into landscape layouts, and geometry constructions with auxiliary lines added. Each chain is verified by the simulator, so every intermediate image is correct by construction. We fine-tune Show-o and Bagel on the corpus and evaluate on held-out instances of each task, on GeoQA and MathVista for understanding, and on WISE for generation from reasoning prompts, reporting accuracy and chain length.
CONTROLS: The same models fine-tuned on text-only versions of the chains in which each visual state is replaced by a textual description of equal content, on final-answer supervision only, on chains with the visual states shuffled across steps, and training on half the corpus.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Interleaved supervision should beat text-described chains on navigation and jigsaw and by less on geometry. If shuffled visual states train as well, the models are ignoring the images and the corpus is working as extra text.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on interleaved chains
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Bagel with group-relative policy optimisation on maze navigation, jigsaw solving and geometry tasks where a simulator checks the final answer, and we extend the reward with a term that checks each intermediate visual state against the simulator's own state after the described step. The model samples eight chains per problem with compact latent visual states, and the policy update uses the verified rewards and a reference-model penalty. We start from a checkpoint that we first fine-tune on a small interleaved corpus, and we measure held-out accuracy, the fraction of chains whose intermediate states pass verification, and chain length over training.
CONTROLS: Supervised fine-tuning alone at the same number of examples, reinforcement learning with the final-answer reward only, the same training on text-only chains, a random reward of equal variance, and the sampling count at four and sixteen.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Intermediate verification should raise accuracy over final-answer reward on navigation and jigsaw, where wrong states compound. If the random reward reaches the same accuracy, the gain comes from sampling and selection rather than from the reward.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Few-step diffusion for intermediate visual states inside one model
PROPOSAL: We build on Transfusion-style training, in which one transformer predicts text tokens and denoises image patches, and we give intermediate visual states a denoising schedule of four steps with a coarse patch size, reserving the full schedule and fine patches for the final image only. The intermediate states are kept in the context as their denoised latent patches rather than being re-encoded, so that the visual part of the chain stays short. We train on synthetic maze navigation and jigsaw chains and on reasoning-driven text-to-image prompts with a planning sketch as intermediate state, and we evaluate task accuracy, GenEval and WISE scores, and tokens per chain.
CONTROLS: The full denoising schedule for every state, a single-step schedule, the model with intermediate states re-encoded by the understanding encoder, text-only chains, and a two-model pipeline with an external diffusion generator.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: Four-step intermediates should keep accuracy within a few points of the full schedule at a fraction of the compute per state, and the sketch state should raise WISE over text-only planning. If the single-step schedule does as well, the intermediate state needs no visual quality at all.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Summarising past visual states into a few learned cache tokens
PROPOSAL: Train Bagel so that, after each visual reasoning step, the thousands of tokens of that visual state are replaced in the key-value cache by thirty-two learned summary tokens produced by a cross-attention module reading the state, while the text tokens stay untouched. Later steps attend to the summaries of all earlier states and to the full tokens of the current state only, which keeps the context nearly linear in the number of steps. Fine-tune the summary module and the model jointly on synthetic maze navigation, jigsaw solving and multi-step instruction-based editing with rendered intermediates, and evaluate held-out accuracy, editing scores on ImgEdit, and throughput against chain length.
CONTROLS: Full tokens kept for every state, summaries of eight and of one hundred twenty-eight tokens, summaries produced by mean pooling without learning, earlier states dropped entirely, and text-only chains.
COST: 850
PREDICTION: Learned summaries should match full retention on tasks that refer back to earlier states, such as editing, and dropping earlier states should hurt there but not on navigation. If mean pooling is as good, the cross-attention module is not needed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How accuracy trades against visual tokens per reasoning step
PROPOSAL: We measure, on one unified model, how the number of visual tokens spent per intermediate state governs both accuracy and chain cost. Starting from Bagel with intermediate states produced by its generator, we vary the tokens per state over sixteen, sixty-four, two hundred fifty-six and one thousand twenty-four by changing the generator's latent resolution, fine-tune each setting on synthetic maze navigation, jigsaw solving and contour-to-landscape chains, and record held-out accuracy, the longest chain length that trains without divergence, and the sequence length and throughput at inference. We fit the resulting curves to find the smallest token count per state at which accuracy saturates for each task family.
CONTROLS: Text-only chains and direct answers as reference points, a setting in which the visual state is produced but masked out of attention, and the same sweep on a second model, Show-o.
COST: 1300
PREDICTION: Accuracy should saturate well below one thousand tokens per state on navigation and jigsaw and later on landscape generation. If the masked-state setting matches the others, the model is not reading its visual states and the curve measures nothing about visual reasoning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Visual planning states for editing and contour-to-landscape generation
PROPOSAL: We test whether interleaved visual states help the generative side of reasoning: for instruction-based editing with several dependent instructions and for landscape generation from topographic contour maps, we train Bagel to produce first a coarse layout state, a low-resolution rendering of regions and their labels, then a textual check of the layout against the instruction or the contour lines, then the final image. The layout state is compact and is kept in context while the final image is not. We fine-tune on rendered pairs of contour maps and terrain, on ImgEdit multi-step edits, and evaluate editing accuracy judged by a separate vision-language model, terrain consistency with the contours measured by slope agreement, and generation throughput.
CONTROLS: Direct generation without the layout state, a text-only plan in place of the layout, the layout state produced but not checked, and generation by a diffusion model conditioned on the contour map without any reasoning.
COST: 950
PREDICTION: The layout state should raise slope agreement and multi-step editing accuracy over direct generation, with the text-only plan in between. If the unchecked layout does as well, the gain comes from the layout itself and not from the verification step.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compact visual tokens for interleaved reasoning on jigsaw and navigation puzzles
PROPOSAL: Finetune Janus-Pro on jigsaw and maze traces in which every visual intermediate is stored as a compact set of 64 tokens produced by a learned pooling layer, while text steps keep their full token count. Train in two stages, first on short traces and then on long ones, and evaluate jigsaw accuracy, maze success and reasoning-driven text-to-image alignment on GenEval and WISE, together with attention cost per step for chains of 4, 8 and 16 images.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same model reasoning with text-only intermediates. Compare against the same model keeping full-length visual tokens at every step. Compare with and without the pooling layer, training on the same traces. Compare across chain lengths that extend beyond the lengths used for training.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Pooled tokens should cut attention cost sharply while keeping jigsaw accuracy close to the full-token model. The idea is falsified when accuracy on chains longer than any seen in training drops back to the text-only level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Staged curriculum for long image-text reasoning chains in a unified model
PROPOSAL: Finetune Show-o on jigsaw and maze traces using a curriculum that raises the number of interleaved images from one up to eight as training proceeds, with each image encoded by a vision tower as 256 tokens and text steps kept at full length. Evaluate jigsaw accuracy, maze success and reasoning-driven text-to-image alignment on GenEval and WISE, together with attention cost per step for chains of 4, 8 and 16 images.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same model reasoning on captioning data. Compare against the same model keeping full-length text tokens at every step. Compare with and without the optimiser warmup, training on the same traces. Compare across image counts that stay within the lengths used for training.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The curriculum should raise jigsaw accuracy while keeping attention cost per step modest. The idea is falsified when accuracy on chains longer than any seen in training drops back to the text-only level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Window-limited attention over visual history for interleaved reasoning
PROPOSAL: Train a Janus-Pro model on VQA, jigsaw and instruction-based editing traces where attention at each step covers only the latest two images plus all text, and a cached summary vector stands in for older images. Evaluate on a held-out jigsaw set, the editing benchmark ImgEdit and visual question answering on MMMU, recording tokens processed per step and accuracy by chain length up to 12 images.
CONTROLS: Compare against full attention over every earlier image on the same traces. Compare keeping the latest one, two or four images while the training data are held the same. Compare with the cached summary replaced by a summary taken from a different chain, using identical weights otherwise. Compare across chain lengths that go beyond training.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Window-limited attention should cut tokens processed per step while holding accuracy on long jigsaw chains close to full attention. The approach is in trouble when swapped summaries score as well as the proper ones.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Recipe tuning for interleaved reasoning with a unified image-text model
PROPOSAL: Train a Show-o model on VQA, jigsaw and instruction-based editing traces with a cosine decay of the optimiser step size, mixed text and image losses weighted at constant ratios and gradient clipping on each update. Evaluate on a held-out jigsaw set, the editing benchmark ImgEdit and visual question answering on MMMU, recording tokens processed per step and accuracy by chain length up to 12 images.
CONTROLS: Compare against full attention with a larger language backbone on the same traces. Compare short, medium and long text steps while the images are held the same. Compare with the optimiser state reset between stages, using identical weights otherwise. Compare across caption styles that stay within training.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The tuned recipe should cut tokens processed per step while holding accuracy on long jigsaw chains close to the larger backbone. The approach is in trouble when the reset optimiser scores as well as the continuous one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent visual thoughts for long navigation chains in a single multimodal model
PROPOSAL: Replace each generated image in the reasoning chain with a handful of continuous latent vectors that a lightweight decoder can expand to pixels only when needed, and train a Bagel-style model on map-navigation and rearrangement traces with 6 to 20 visual steps. Evaluate path success and rearrangement accuracy, plus peak training footprint and generation time per chain.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same model emitting full images at each step of the long chains. Compare chains of 16 to 20 visual steps with the latent version and the text-only version. Compare with and without the decoder expansion, reading the same traces. Compare across chain lengths covering the whole range met in the tasks.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Latent thoughts should lower training footprint and generation time on the longest chains while keeping path success near the full-image model. The idea is refuted when success on the longest chains falls to the text-only level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuous image summaries for map navigation and rearrangement reasoning
PROPOSAL: Condense every drawn picture into a small block of continuous codes, expanded to pixels by a light decoder on demand only, and fit a Janus-style model on route-finding and object-rearrangement traces having 6 to 20 visual steps. Score route success and rearrangement accuracy, plus peak training footprint and wall-clock generation time for each chain.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same model emitting full images at each step of the short chains. Compare chains of 1 to 3 visual steps with the latent version and the text-only version. Compare with and without the decoder expansion, reading the same traces. Compare across chain lengths covering only the shortest part of the range met in the tasks.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Image summaries should lower training footprint and generation time on the shortest chains while keeping path success near the full-image model. The idea is refuted when success on the shortest chains falls to the text-only level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient-stable joint training for interleaved text and image reasoning
PROPOSAL: Train a unified model on interleaved traces using separate loss weights for text tokens and image tokens, with the image weight raised gradually over the first stage and gradients clipped per modality. Run 3 repeats of each recipe, and measure final jigsaw accuracy, reasoning-driven text-to-image alignment on WISE and instruction-based editing quality on ImgEdit, alongside the gradient norm trace.
CONTROLS: Measure jigsaw accuracy for the unified model trained with a single shared loss weight. Measure jigsaw accuracy for the model with the image weight switched on from the first step. Measure jigsaw accuracy with and without per-modality clipping, using identical data otherwise. Measure jigsaw accuracy on chains longer than those seen in training.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: Separate weights with gradual ramp-up should give smoother gradient norms and higher final jigsaw accuracy than the shared weight. The recipe is falsified when long-chain accuracy matches the shared-weight model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modality-balanced optimisation for unified image-text chain-of-thought training
PROPOSAL: Optimise a single multimodal model on interleaved traces with distinct objective weights for word tokens and picture tokens, bringing the picture weight up slowly in the early phase and clipping gradient magnitude within each modality. Run 3 repeats of each recipe, and measure final text-to-image alignment on WISE, jigsaw accuracy and editing quality on ImgEdit, alongside the gradient norm trace.
CONTROLS: Measure training loss for the unified model trained with a single shared loss weight. Measure training loss for the model with the image weight switched on from the first step. Measure training loss with and without per-modality clipping, using identical data otherwise. Measure training loss on chains drawn from the training set.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: Separate weights with gradual ramp-up should give smoother gradient norms and lower final training loss than the shared weight. The recipe is falsified when training loss on seen chains matches the shared-weight model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: One-model interleaved reasoning versus a coupled generator pipeline for jigsaw solving
PROPOSAL: Train a single Janus-Pro model end to end on jigsaw traces that alternate piece-arrangement text with rendered intermediate boards, and judge it on the coherence of consecutive boards, scored by a pixel-overlap check between each predicted board and the board implied by the previous move, plus final puzzle accuracy on three-by-three and four-by-four grids using 1000 held-out puzzles.
CONTROLS: Compare against a pipeline in which a separate image generator draws each board for a text-only reasoner. Compare against the same single model reasoning in text alone. Compare with and without the pixel-overlap check, scored on the same traces. Compare across puzzle grids that increase in difficulty.
COST: 560
PREDICTION: The single model should score higher board coherence than the pipeline while matching its final accuracy. The idea is falsified when coherence is the same for both on larger grids.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: End-to-end captioned reasoning traces for jigsaw solving in a unified model
PROPOSAL: Train a single Show-o model end to end on jigsaw traces that alternate move descriptions with written scene captions, and judge it on the fluency of consecutive captions, scored by a text-overlap check between each predicted caption and the caption implied by the previous move, plus final puzzle accuracy on three-by-three and four-by-four grids using 1000 held-out puzzles.
CONTROLS: Compare against another single model trained end to end on captioning traces. Compare against the same single model reasoning with pieces of a different puzzle. Compare with and without the board-count marker, scored on the same traces. Compare across puzzle themes that stay at one difficulty.
COST: 560
PREDICTION: The single model should score higher caption fluency than the captioning model while matching its final accuracy. The idea is falsified when fluency is the same for both on larger grids.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Emitting only the changed image tokens at each reasoning step
PROPOSAL: We train Show-o to represent each intermediate visual state by the discrete image tokens that differ from the previous state together with their positions, a learned detector choosing the positions, while a small state cache outside the attention context holds the full current state for reconstruction. A maze move or a jigsaw swap then costs a few tokens and a full redraw stays possible when the detector marks every position. Training uses simulated navigation, jigsaw and contour-to-landscape chains, and we report held-out accuracy, visual tokens per step and reconstruction fidelity.
CONTROLS: Full-image interleaving at equal data, text-only chains, direct answers, a random subset of positions of the same size as the detector's choice, the cache disabled so that changes must be inferred from context, and the detector threshold at two values, over three seeds.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Change encoding should cut visual tokens per step by an order of magnitude on navigation and jigsaw at equal accuracy and lose fidelity on landscape chains where most pixels change. If the random subset matches it, position selection is not the ingredient that matters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reinforcement learning on verbalised state descriptions for visual tasks
PROPOSAL: We strengthen the textual reasoning of Qwen2.5-VL on maze navigation, jigsaw solving and geometry by group-relative policy optimisation with simulator-checked final answers, where every chain must describe the visual state after each step in a fixed textual schema, grid coordinates for mazes, piece placements for jigsaws and point coordinates for geometry, so that transitions are tracked in words without producing any image. Eight chains are sampled per problem and the schema is enforced by a format reward. We report held-out accuracy, the share of chains whose described states match the simulator, and chain length.
CONTROLS: Supervised fine-tuning on schema-formatted chains at the same number of examples, the same training without the format reward, free-form chains as the floor, the final-answer reward only, and a pipeline that renders the described states with an external generator for visualisation only, over three seeds.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Schema-formatted chains should beat free-form ones on navigation and jigsaw and the state-match share should rise over training. On geometry the schema may be too coarse and the gain may vanish there.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Coarse few-step denoising for intermediate visual states
PROPOSAL: We train one transformer that predicts text tokens and denoises image patches, in the Transfusion style, giving intermediate visual states a four-step denoising schedule with coarse patches and the final image the full schedule with fine patches, and keeping intermediates in context as denoised latents without re-encoding. The patch size for intermediates is twice that of the final image. Training data are synthetic navigation and jigsaw chains plus reasoning-driven text-to-image prompts with a planning sketch as intermediate. We report task accuracy, GenEval and WISE, FID of final images against reference renders, and tokens per chain.
CONTROLS: The full schedule for every state, a single-step schedule, intermediates re-encoded by the understanding encoder, chains of text alone, and a written plan in place of the sketch, over three seeds.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: Four-step intermediates should stay within a few points of the full schedule on accuracy at a fraction of the compute per state, and the sketch should lift WISE over planning in words. If one step suffices, visual quality of intermediates is irrelevant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pairing an understanding model with a video generator for state transitions
PROPOSAL: We connect Qwen2.5-VL, which plans each reasoning step in text, to an open video generation model conditioned on the current image and the planned step, which renders the next visual state as a short clip whose last frame is fed back to the understanding model. The generator is fine-tuned on rendered transitions from synthetic navigation and jigsaw simulators, with a learned gate deciding when a visual update is worth requesting. We evaluate held-out accuracy on navigation, jigsaw and geometry, GenEval and WISE for generation prompts, and latency per chain of the two-model pipeline.
CONTROLS: The planner alone with text-only chains, the planner with a still-image generator instead of video, the gate always open, the gate always closed, the gate replaced by a random coin as placebo, the clip length at two values, and the generator without fine-tuning on transitions, over three seeds.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: Video-rendered transitions should help on navigation where motion is natural and little on geometry. If the still-image generator does as well, temporal rendering adds nothing beyond the state itself.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Replacing each finished visual state by learned summary tokens
PROPOSAL: We train Bagel so that once a visual reasoning step is complete, its thousands of state tokens are swapped in the key-value cache for thirty-two summary tokens produced by a cross-attention reader, text tokens staying as they are, so that later steps see full tokens for the current state only and summaries for the rest. We fine-tune the reader and model jointly on synthetic navigation, jigsaw and multi-step editing chains with rendered intermediates and report held-out accuracy, ImgEdit scores and throughput against chain length.
CONTROLS: Full tokens kept for every state, summaries of eight and of one hundred twenty-eight tokens, mean-pooled summaries without learning, earlier states dropped entirely, text-only chains, a pipeline with an external editor per step, and Bagel's published ImgEdit score as a sanity check, over three seeds.
COST: 850
PREDICTION: Learned summaries should equal full retention on editing, which refers back to earlier states, while dropping states should hurt there and not on navigation. If mean pooling is as good, the learned reader is not needed and the result is a plain compression story.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tool-augmented visual reasoning with cropping, drawing and plotting operations
PROPOSAL: We equip Janus-Pro with a set of callable image operations, crop and zoom, draw a line or marker, overlay a grid, plot a function, and fine-tune it on chains where each step either reasons in text or calls one operation whose output image is appended to the context. Each operation returns an image at the input resolution. Training chains come from synthetic navigation, jigsaw and geometry problems annotated with the operation sequence a solver would use. We report held-out accuracy, the number of calls per chain and the fraction of calls whose output is referred to in later text.
CONTROLS: The same model with text-only chains, calls allowed but outputs withheld from the context, each operation removed in turn, and a random operation inserted at each call, over three seeds.
COST: 850
PREDICTION: Operations should help most on geometry, where auxiliary lines matter, and least on jigsaw, where pieces must move globally. If withholding outputs costs nothing, the model is not reading the images it requests and the claim fails.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compact layout states for reasoning-driven generation and editing
PROPOSAL: We train Bagel to produce, for multi-step instruction editing and for landscape generation from contour maps, a coarse layout state first, a low-resolution map of regions and labels, then a textual check of that layout against the instruction or the contours, then the final image, keeping only the layout in context. Fine-tuning uses rendered contour-terrain pairs and ImgEdit multi-step edits, and we evaluate editing accuracy judged by a separate vision-language model, Qwen2.5-VL, slope agreement between terrain and contours, and generation throughput.
CONTROLS: Direct generation without the layout, a text-only plan in place of the layout, the layout produced but never checked, a diffusion model conditioned on the contour map without reasoning, and the layout at two resolutions, over three seeds.
COST: 950
PREDICTION: The layout state should raise slope agreement and multi-step editing accuracy over direct generation with the text plan in between. If the unchecked layout does as well, the check adds nothing and the gain is the layout alone.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-model reranking of generated images for reasoning prompts
PROPOSAL: We train a reward model on human preference pairs for reasoning-driven generation prompts, images judged on whether they satisfy the implicit constraints of the prompt, and use it to rerank sixteen samples from Bagel for each prompt, then fine-tune Bagel by direct preference optimisation on the reward model's rankings. The same reward model scores edits on ImgEdit by comparing the edited image with the instruction. We report WISE and GenEval, the reward model's agreement with held-out human judgements, and editing accuracy.
CONTROLS: Bagel without reranking, reranking with an off-the-shelf aesthetic scorer, the preference optimisation without the reranking pipeline, a reward model trained on shuffled labels as placebo, and the reward model trained on half the pairs, over three seeds.
COST: 950
PREDICTION: Reranking should raise WISE by a few points and preference optimisation should keep most of that gain without sampling. If the aesthetic scorer gives the same lift, the reward model is not capturing reasoning constraints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A persistent latent canvas edited in place across reasoning steps
PROPOSAL: We give Show-o a latent canvas of two hundred fifty-six tokens that stands for the current visual state and is rewritten in place at each step by edit tokens the model generates, so that the context holds the text and one canvas rather than a growing stack of images. A decoder renders the canvas for inspection and for the final image. We fine-tune on simulated navigation, jigsaw and contour-to-landscape chains and report held-out accuracy, tokens per chain and the fidelity of the rendered canvas to the simulator state.
CONTROLS: Full-image interleaving at equal data, chains without visual states, the canvas reset at each step instead of edited, random edit tokens, sampling temperature at two values, and a pipeline with an external generator, over three seeds.
COST: 750
PREDICTION: The canvas should hold accuracy at constant context size on navigation and jigsaw and fall behind on landscape chains that rewrite most of the canvas. If resetting matches editing, persistence is not what helps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: High-resolution tiled perception with textual reasoning for visual problems
PROPOSAL: We replace the vision encoder of Qwen2.5-VL with a dynamic tiling scheme that splits each input image into up to sixteen tiles encoded at native resolution plus a global thumbnail, and fine-tune the model on text-only chains for maze navigation, jigsaw solving and geometry whose steps describe the visual content in words. The chains come from the same simulators with the intermediate states rendered as text, and we report held-out accuracy, accuracy as a function of input image size, and the model's localisation error on a probing task that asks for coordinates of maze cells and puzzle pieces.
CONTROLS: The original encoder at fixed resolution, tiling without the thumbnail, the number of tiles at three values, direct answers without chains, and the probing task on images downsampled by half, over three seeds.
COST: 750
PREDICTION: Tiled perception should cut localisation error and lift accuracy on large mazes and fine geometry. If the gain vanishes on small images, perception rather than reasoning was the bottleneck and the claim of a reasoning gain is refuted for those tasks.
